program_overview.title: Ethical Hacking and Cybersecurity Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: Break in so you can defend: authorized penetration testing taught the professional way, from networking and Linux to red team operations and reports that get vulnerabilities fixed.
program_overview.description:
Ethical hacking is authorized, legal security testing done to find and fix weaknesses before criminals do, and the emphasis in this course is on the word ethical. It is built for people who want a real cybersecurity career, penetration tester, security analyst, red or blue team engineer, and it starts every offensive skill from a foundation of authorization, scope and law. The path is complete and in order: networking, Linux and programming for security, reconnaissance and scanning, then core exploitation, web and network attacks, Metasploit, the OWASP Top 10, post-exploitation, all practised only in lab environments and authorized ranges, then advanced work: buffer overflows and mitigation bypasses, cryptography, red team operations, and the defensive side, DevSecOps, threat hunting, incident response and forensics, so you understand both attack and defence. A finale month runs a full authorized penetration test of a lab and writes the professional report, then sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of lab practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.
what_makes_this_different: Ethics and authorization first, not as a footnote: scope, consent and law frame every technique
Everything practised in labs and authorized ranges only, never against systems you do not own
Both sides taught: offensive skills and the defensive DevSecOps, threat-hunting and forensics response
Professional reporting is a core skill: findings that actually get fixed, not just exploits
An honest 10-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this ethical hacking course cover?
faqs.answer: The full authorized-pentesting path in order: networking, Linux and programming for security, reconnaissance and OSINT, scanning and vulnerability assessment; then core exploitation, system, web (OWASP Top 10) and network attacks, Metasploit, post-exploitation and advanced domains like Active Directory, mobile and cloud; then advanced offensive work (exploit development, mitigation bypasses, red team) and the defensive side (DevSecOps, threat hunting, incident response, forensics). A finale month runs a full authorized lab pentest, writes the professional report and sits the final exam. Everything is practised only in labs and authorized ranges.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn ethical hacking properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Is ethical hacking legal, and is this course legal to take?
faqs.answer: Ethical hacking is legal precisely because it is authorized: you test only systems you own or have written permission to test, within an agreed scope. That principle is taught from the first week and enforced throughout, and all practical work happens in dedicated lab environments and authorized ranges we provide. Using these skills against systems without permission is a crime, and this course exists to build defenders and professional testers, not to enable that.

faqs.question: Do I need prior experience to start?
faqs.answer: No. The course begins with networking, Linux and programming foundations and builds from there. What matters most is genuine curiosity, patience for problem-solving, and a commitment to using these skills legally and ethically. It is an adult course aimed at serious career-changers and IT professionals.

faqs.question: Will this get me a certification like CEH or OSCP?
faqs.answer: This course is not an exam voucher for CEH or OSCP, and we are honest about that: it teaches the skills those certifications test and prepares you thoroughly to pursue them next. You earn a Modern Age Coders certificate here by passing the final exam, which includes a real authorized lab pentest and its report, exactly the kind of work the industry certifications and employers care about.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
